judge_self_preference.note: This comparison cannot be judged by one model without the judge's own identity deciding it. The prior tier study measured its Opus 5 judge scoring its own family +0.31 on calibration and +0.78 on substance while the deterministic band-agreement margin moved only -0.026 - i.e. the judge-scored margin was mostly preference. A GPT judge has the mirror problem. So both are used: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5 (which is ALSO a candidate here, the strongest possible form of the conflict, and is expected to favour Claude) and openai.gpt-5.5 (NOT a candidate - the candidates are the 5.6 variants - but same family and vendor, so expected to favour GPT). Where the two agree, the finding survives both biases and is reported as established. Where they disagree, the axis is reported as NOT ESTABLISHED and no recommendation rests on it. Neither margin is 'corrected' by subtracting a bias estimate: that would produce a number that looks adjusted and was never measured. The deterministic layers - band agreement, anti-false-positive escalation, grounding, output contract - involve no judge at all and are what the recommendation actually rests on.

deterministic_cross_check.note: computed with no judge involved. A judge-scored margin unaccompanied by a deterministic margin in the same direction is more likely preference than quality.

length_gap.method: paired by (application, domain); only cells where BOTH models produced a readable analysis are compared. 'signals cited' counts the payload's own signal names (identifier or de-underscored prose form), so a model is not rewarded for writing in identifiers. Reported pooled AND per agent, because pooling four agents can cancel out the one that motivated the question.
length_gap.reading: chars_ratio well above signals_cited_ratio and grounded_ratio means the longer (Claude) analysis is padding: same evidence, more words. chars_ratio at or below those ratios means the shorter (GPT) analysis really is dropping evidence, which outweighs any latency or cost win.

verdict.contract_notes: Prompt says "Return only final analysis"; output adds a document title, a bolded "VERDICT: HIGH RISK" header line, and a 6-item recommended-actions block (SAR filing, dealer suspension) beyond analysis. Numeric alert IDs cited verbatim ("alert 66", "alert 64", "Alert 4", "Alert 104"). Heavy markdown tables/bold; no emoji.
verdict.justification: Band matches RNG-014 and for the right reasons. Each primary signal is validated against paired context, not asserted: address reuse is "5 of 6 SSNs at the same unit number... no shared surnames" (exact-unit, the customer's own carve-out), phone reuse "5 different surnames, 4 first seen in last 90 days" plus same-dealer convergence, email "4 different surnames... 6-week window". Employer count 9 is explicitly conceded as benign alone and only counted because "7 funneled to one dealer and 3 sharing the borrower's phone". Section 5 rejects the exact benign explanations the customer names (multi-unit density, family sharing, large employer, consortium volume, normalization error) and correctly refuses to lean on the 1,180 apps/yr dealer volume as a driver. Corroboration is independent of the overlap: 9-year DOB spread on one SSN and a 2-month AU-built file at age 57. Section 2 explicitly argues the identifiers cross-link rather than being one behaviour counted four times — the rule-2 test. Deductions: §5 largely re-litigates the "Not explainable" column of §1 and §6 recaps both, so some length is non-load-bearing; the fraud_score 999 / LTV / income items are asserted as fraud weight with no context validation and are secondary to the rings domain.

verdict.contract_notes: Title correct, no emojis, no alert numbers cited (refers to "the alert finding"). Bolded "Classification: LOW RISK" line sits outside the specified output shape, and the LOW RISK body plus multi-clause recommendation runs at/over the 3-5 sentence cap for a clearing verdict.
verdict.justification: Pinned band is POSSIBLE RISK on SYN-008 (3+ states in a short timeframe). The analysis reads the same fact — "3 locations across CO, UT and NM within 90 days" — and clears it. Worse, it names a second independent pattern and then waves it off: the "shared email address linked to two recently-created identities with different surnames ... stands alone", while also conceding "no lease or utility record corroborates any of the three addresses" and a stated-vs-verified income gap ($79,000 vs $64,800). That is multi-state variation + unrelated-identity email reuse + unverifiable residence, i.e. exactly the corroborated combination the POSSIBLE band describes, so the mitigation (employer project sites, 134-month file) is over-weighted. Context validation itself is genuine and dense — this is a well-argued wrong answer, not thin reasoning.

caveats: This comparison cannot be judged by one model without the judge's own identity deciding it. The prior tier study measured its Opus 5 judge scoring its own family +0.31 on calibration and +0.78 on substance while the deterministic band-agreement margin moved only -0.026 - i.e. the judge-scored margin was mostly preference. A GPT judge has the mirror problem. So both are used: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5 (which is ALSO a candidate here, the strongest possible form of the conflict, and is expected to favour Claude) and openai.gpt-5.5 (NOT a candidate - the candidates are the 5.6 variants - but same family and vendor, so expected to favour GPT). Where the two agree, the finding survives both biases and is reported as established. Where they disagree, the axis is reported as NOT ESTABLISHED and no recommendation rests on it. Neither margin is 'corrected' by subtracting a bias estimate: that would produce a number that looks adjusted and was never measured. The deterministic layers - band agreement, anti-false-positive escalation, grounding, output contract - involve no judge at all and are what the recommendation actually rests on.

The recommendation rests on the DETERMINISTIC layers - band agreement against the pinned fixture, escalation on the anti-false-positive fixtures, _context grounding, and agents.output_contract.check. The judged calibration and substance scores are subjective and are reported separately, and an axis where the two judges disagree yields no finding at all.
6 applications per cell. A band-agreement difference of one case is 17 points, so a one-case gap between two models is inside this sample's resolution by construction.

Only 2 of the 5 anti-false-positive fixtures (APP-1009, APP-1010) exercise the four agents swept here; APP-1006/1007/1008 target employment, dealer and income, which were not swept. The false-positive finding is therefore narrow and a wider anti-FP sweep is the obvious next measurement.
Percentiles come from evals.bench.summarize_values: p50 needs 5 samples, p95 needs 20. Cells below those counts report the refusal, not a number.

GPT specialists receive the verbatim prompt concatenated with the user turn (the mantle Responses shape agents.synthesize already uses), while Claude specialists receive it as a cached system prompt. That is a real difference in how the two families are invoked and it cannot be removed while GPT-5.x is off Converse.
Latency and cost here are single serial calls, not the fan-out. The end-to-end consequence of a swap belongs to the pipeline benchmark.
